catalog_quote: 2.3 Accent. Kolyma Yukaghir has a fixed stress accent. If a multisyllabic word contains one or more CVV/CVCC/CVVC syllables, a stress falls on the rightmost CVV/CVCC/CVVC syllable: ˈʃoo.loq 'ashes'; ar.nuu.ˈjaa 'wolverine'; mun.ˈdejk 'go for (sth)'; ku.ˈruul.buj 'always'. Otherwise, a bisyllabic word has its stress on the first syllable, and a trisyllabic word and a word with more syllables have their stress on the second syllable: ˈnu.me 'house'; ˈto.low 'wild reindeer'; t'ol.ˈʁo.ro 'hare'; o.ˈʁun.bej '(it) got wet'. audit.recode_to: No change to classification weight / edge=unbounded (rightmost heavy), which every source states. Pending Nikolaeva 1998 / Maslova 2003:58-60, consider reclassification the sub-fields to the majority/primary-phonologist analysis: heavy = CVV + CVC (what counts as heavy 'CVV+CVC'), default-when-no-heavy = final (default-to-same-edge), with lexical (C)VCe disyllables initial; keep Nagasaki 2010's CVC-light / initial-second default as the documented minority variant in the primary-stress rule/caution.

sources.quote: 'Ударение разноместное, не смыслоразличительное, зависит от структуры слова, а именно: ударение падает на последний тяжелый слог (слог с долгим гласным или закрытый слог типа CVC) в словоформе; при отсутствии тяжелых слогов ударение располагается на последнем слоге словоформы. Например: šoromə́ «человек», jel'ōd'ə «солнце», önmēdē «молодая лиственница», ńánmə «тальник».' sources.quote: No stress rule stated. Incidental: '/e/ は，アクセントの置かれない位置で弱化して［ə］となる' (/e/ reduces to [ə] in unaccented position), e.g. n'a:če [njá:tʃə] 'face' (stress on the long-vowel syllable); čuge 'road' pronounced [tʃúge ~ tʃúgə] (initial stress in a light (C)VCe disyllable, matching Nagasaki's disyllabic default and Maslova's (C)VCe exception class). Also reports Nikolaeva 1997:149 that vowel length in CVCə/CVCCə words is 'fully predictable from word structure'.

sources.note: The only dedicated article on Kolyma Yukaghir prosodic structure, by the primary phonologist whose analysis Maslova 2003 and StressTyp2 follow; it should settle whether plain CVC is heavy and what the no-heavy default is, the two points on which our Nagasaki-based sub-coding (what counts as heavy: CVV, default initial/second) conflicts with the Nikolaeva/Maslova tradition (CVC heavy, default final).
